MINOR | ledger_sha256 is labelled canonical JSON but does not follow the module's own frozen canonical form. diagnostic_inputs.py:191-192 re-implements the serializer inline and omits the terminal LF, while diagnostic_basis.canonical_intent:56-57 and r2 ('Canonical JSON bytes will be ... + \n, with exactly one terminal LF') define canonical bytes as including it; manifest['ledger_digest_scope'] nonetheless asserts 'canonical-json:...'. An independent verifier re-deriving the ledger digest under the frozen rule gets a different value, and test_diagnostic_inputs.py:172 only re-copies the same inline expression, so the divergence is untestable by construction. Remedy: serialize the ledger through canonical_intent-equivalent bytes (or relabel the scope as json-compact-sorted-no-terminal-lf) and assert against the shared helper, not a duplicated dumps call.

MINOR | Rights evidence is the only unbounded, recursion-unguarded input, and it breaks the module's ValueError refusal contract. _rights:133-136 accepts whatever the caller's resolver returns with no length bound (contrast :58 1 MB spec, diagnostic_mesh.py:44 100 kB mesh, :182 1 MB sources, MAX_SOURCE_NODES) and passes it to strict_json, which catches only TypeError/UnicodeError/JSONDecodeError (diagnostic_basis.py:32). A deeply nested payload (e.g. b'['*100000 + b']'*100000) raises RecursionError out of build_bundle, so the permission path - the input class the design treats as least trusted - is the least bounded. Remedy: bound evidence length and catch RecursionError (or pre-scan nesting) in strict_json, with a fixture.
